statement.essentials: Inside the gland the nerve usually lies on the outer side of a large vein, which scans use to estimate where the nerve runs.
statement.anatomy: The retromandibular vein runs down through the gland and marks the division between its deep and superficial lobes, so it approximates the depth of the facial nerve. The lower division of the nerve usually lies lateral (superficial) to it.
statement.clinical: The vein was deep or medial to the marginal mandibular branch or lower division in 77.1% of 35 parotidectomies, and in 92.6% of 1,454 sides across the literature and that cohort. The nerve ran medial to the vein in 3 of 49 donor bodies.

limitations: The relation is not constant; the authors stress that the vein is a landmark, not a guarantee. The model draws the usual relation.
